dedupe_keys.name: v soft communications fmcommander fm allocation and coverage software

description: FMCommander is desktop software from V-Soft Communications for FM radio engineering under the rules of the US Federal Communications Commission. It combines contour-to-contour and FCC minimum-separation study engines with interactive mapping, so that engineers can find upgrade opportunities for stations, evaluate short-spaced moves, place translators and boosters and model low-power FM (LPFM) facilities. It draws on the same polygon mapping database as V-Soft's Probe and AM-Pro packages to produce FCC coverage and interference maps, includes an antenna pattern editor that builds directional patterns, a terrain profiler and population counts, and has been updated with 2020 US Census data and extended LPFM features. V-Soft also sells Probe 5 for Longley-Rice and other propagation predictions, AM-Pro for AM allocations, Microwave Pro, FCC TVStudy tools, and terrain, land-cover and census databases. Coverage: the United States, with a Canadian version. Format and access: commercial Windows software, priced by use, with training services. Caveats: proprietary; FCC contour methods describe regulatory coverage, not measured reception. Simulation uses: coverage of FM stations for emergency alerting and population reach, and scenarios of coverage lost when transmitters go off air. Related records: the FCC LMS and CDBS databases supply station data, and the FCC propagation curves define the contours.
